questions.q: Which agency is responsible for establishing India's 'National Caregiver Registry' as per the latest NITI Aayog recommendations?
options: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
questions.explain: Centralized registries like this are meant to professionalize and track the caregiving workforce across the nation. Once implemented, this would be a major milestone in ensuring that caregivers get the quality standards and recognition they rightly deserve in the formal job market.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.q: Which official chairs the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.explain: The RBI Governor leads this committee, which holds the primary responsibility of setting interest rates to maintain price stability. It's a critical body established under the RBI Act to keep inflation within a mandated target range, ensuring our economy stays on a steady path.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.q: Regarding the recent classification of Tata Sons as an NBFC-Upper Layer (NBFC-UL), which of these statements accurately reflects the current regulatory position?
options: The company is now required to list on stock exchanges regardless of any ongoing legal petitions.
This classification marks its formal transition into a Tier-1 commercial bank by 2027.
Tata Sons was granted an automatic exemption from the Scale Based Regulation (SBR) framework.
Its status as an NBFC-UL remains subject to the final decision on its pending de-registration application.
questions.explain: Clearly, the RBI has included them as an Upper Layer entity while their de-registration request is still being reviewed. If that request gets approved later, they might just bypass the mandatory listing requirement. You should know that NBFC-UL status is governed by RBI’s SBR framework, which aims to prevent systemic risks akin to those monitored in banks under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.q: Which specific criterion is primary for identifying a 'standalone' entity as an NBFC-Upper Layer under the latest RBI guidelines?
options: Total assets valued at Rs. 1,00,000 crore or more
A history of 20 years in operation
questions.explain: Hitting that massive one-lakh crore mark in assets effectively triggers this classification, according to the RBI's simplified identification metrics. These stringent layers were brought in to manage 'shadow banks' whose potential collapse could trigger wider market turmoil. It's essentially about ensuring that entities large enough to impact the economy operate with capital buffers comparable to those of traditional lenders.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.q: A key concern regarding the selection process of the Rs. 1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund involves which of the following?
options: The total lack of technological innovation among chosen entities
Potential conflicts of interest due to investment links between committee members and selected firms
The fund’s total reliance on high-interest commercial debt rather than equity
Failure to target companies operating at a TRL-4 maturity level
questions.explain: Reports indicate that a surprising number of selected companies share investment history with those sitting on the selection board. Such scrutiny is vital because the RDI Fund functions under the ANRF, a statutory body set up via the Ministry of Science and Technology. Safeguarding public capital against cronyism is a recurring theme in government procurement oversight.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.q: The proposed amendment to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, aims to reintroduce which fee structure on UPI transactions?
questions.explain: Essentially, this bill could allow providers to charge merchants a percentage-based fee for digital payments above a certain turnover. While users might worry about a 'UPI tax,' the Ministry clarifies it’s designed as a business-to-bank fee to help cover the massive infrastructure costs involved. Keep in mind that India's digital payment ecosystem has thrived under zero-MDR, but banks argue current subsidies don't fully recover their maintenance expenses.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The closure of nearly 94,000 government schools in India over the past decade is largely attributed by experts to demographic shifts and _________.
options: The complete privatization of elementary education
The failure of the Right to Education Act, 2009
Mandatory state-level bans on primary education
The rapid decline in the Total Fertility Rate (TFR)
questions.explain: Demographically speaking, as our fertility rate dips below replacement levels, there are simply fewer children in the school-going age bracket. Schools aren't just shuttering randomly; many states are consolidating smaller institutions into larger 'school complexes' as suggested by the NEP 2020. This shift highlights a transition where efficiency in resources is being prioritized over maintaining extremely small, possibly under-equipped rural centers.

questions.q: Which of the following is true about the historic Dhabaleswar Temple located in Odisha?
options: It strictly follows the Dravidian architectural style.
It is a UNESCO World Heritage site dedicated to Lord Vishnu.
The temple is situated on an island in the Mahanadi river.
It was constructed in the early 20th century by colonial architects.
questions.explain: Perched on an island, this ancient Shiva shrine showcases beautiful Kalinga-style architecture. Its history stretches back over a thousand years, though later rulers were responsible for the structural form we see today. Notably, its two-tiered roof made of terracotta tiles makes it a standout site for researchers of Odisha's temple history.

questions.q: The Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science (SPoCS) is implemented by which nodal agency?
options: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)
questions.explain: Under the Ministry of Culture's direction, this body manages the creation of innovative hubs and planetariums to spark scientific interest in the public. It’s an outreach-heavy initiative meant to decentralize science education outside of traditional classrooms. The organization functions as an autonomous society dedicated specifically to the promotion of scientific culture across the nation.

questions.q: What is the conservation status of the Himalayan serow according to the IUCN Red List?
questions.explain: This elusive mountain herbivore was recently spotted again in Himachal, giving conservationists a reason to celebrate after a long absence. Being listed as 'Near Threatened,' it faces significant risks from shrinking habitats and illegal hunting. These creatures are protected under Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, ensuring they get the highest level of legal safeguards in India.

questions.q: Which river forms a protected estuarine area near Chennai, home to significant marine life and bird species?

questions.q: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) is a neurological disorder primarily affecting which cells in the human body?

It's often referred to as Lou Gehrig's disease, a name that's become globally synonymous with the condition. Medical science hasn't found a cure yet, though current research into environmental factors like pesticide exposure is gaining serious traction.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.q: What is a unique operational feature of the Mullaperiyar Dam despite its physical location in Kerala?
options: Water usage is strictly restricted to irrigation within Kerala alone.
It is fully managed by a central government authority.
Electricity generation is prohibited by interstate law.
Operational control rests with the government of Tamil Nadu.
questions.explain: Even though it's situated within Idukki, the dam is operated by Tamil Nadu under a long-standing historical lease from the British era. This unique arrangement is a major source of friction between the two states due to safety concerns. You should note that its construction utilized traditional materials like Surkhi, which was a standard mortar technique in the 19th century.

questions.q: The National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) provides financial support to students starting from which grade level?

While selection happens based on an eighth-grade test, the actual scholarship awardees begin receiving their funding once they reach Class IX. questions.q: What is the primary objective of the GOBARdhan Scheme introduced by the Union Cabinet?
options: To provide direct solar subsidies for agricultural pump sets
To replace all LPG connections with charcoal-based fuel
To develop a nationwide circular waste-to-energy ecosystem for biogas
To encourage fossil fuel extraction in coastal regions

questions.q: The Agni-4 missile, recently test-fired by India, is categorized as which type of weapon system?
questions.explain: Built by the DRDO, this surface-to-surface weapon is a pillar of India's strategic deterrent. Its ability to be moved on road-mobile launchers makes it incredibly versatile for deployment during a crisis.

questions.q: The Pakal Dul Hydroelectric Project, currently under construction, is being built on a tributary of which major river?

questions.q: The USTR recently flagged concerns about India's UPI ecosystem primarily due to:

Excessive reliance on Chinese server infrastructure
Perceived disadvantages for American electronic payment suppliers
The complete prohibition of all foreign-owned fintech firms

A custodian body created within the ANRF for managing RDI resources
A grant-based foundation managed by private stock brokers

questions.q: In the context of the Indian education landscape, what is the core benefit of school 'consolidation' as promoted by the NEP 2020?

Pooling resources into composite institutions to improve educational quality
Reducing costs by forcing students into private institutions
Eliminating the need for school teachers

It’s an attempt to ensure that 'neighbourhood schools' are actually functional centers of learning. questions.q: What is the primary role of the Ring Laser Gyro-based Inertial Navigation System (RINS) in missiles like Agni-4?
options: Remote detonation from the command center
Ensuring pinpoint accuracy through precision guidance
questions.explain: This complex navigation tech allows the missile to map its path in real-time, drastically reducing its Circular Error Probability (CEP). The system essentially makes the weapon less reliant on external data, keeping it resistant to jamming attempts.

questions.q: For the GOBARdhan scheme, what specific 'blending obligation' is introduced for City Gas Distribution entities?

A complete mandate to remove all CNG stations

questions.q: Regarding the recent disclosures by companies like OpenAI and Meta, what primarily distinguishes these autonomous AI agents from traditional Large Language Models (LLMs)?
options: Agents lack the capability to process complex internet-based data
Agents are confined to responding only to user prompts without internal planning
Agents cannot interact with external systems like email or financial software
Agents possess goal-oriented autonomy and can independently execute multi-step tasks

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the 'alignment failure' view concerning the unintended behavior of AI agents during cybersecurity evaluations?
options: The agent deviated from its assigned goals while attempting to solve problems
The AI system became corrupted by malicious code injected into its software stack
The model lacked the necessary computing power to complete its intended tasks
The system failed to defend against external hackers targeting the infrastructure
questions.explain: Sometimes AI agents 'drift' away from their original instructions, pursuing tasks in ways developers never meant for them to happen. options: Heavy concentration in select sectors with persistently weak consumer demand
A significant decline in private sector infrastructure spending
An overwhelming reliance on government capital expenditure rather than private funds
The complete stagnation of IT-enabled services despite global demand

Polysilicon is the most abundant raw material found in the Thar desert
Domestic module manufacturers have already achieved 100% self-sufficiency in wafers
Complete import reliance for this upstream material creates a supply chain vulnerability

It is specifically designed for single-use heavy-lift launch vehicles only
It employs Full-Flow Staged Combustion (FFSC) technology for improved efficiency
It uses solid fuel instead of liquid propellants for higher thrust

Traditional healthcare practices and the role of indigenous knowledge
Universal high-tech surgery requirements in forest regions

Climate change resulting in the collapse of local insect populations
They were hunted as pests by local farmers
Mass deforestation of their natural breeding grounds in the Himalayas

It is predominantly flat, oval-shaped, and features coral beaches

Increasing the velocity of the radioactive beams
Absorbing remnants from primary heavy-ion beams after hitting targets

The percentage of energy derived solely from offshore wind
